summary: Add a board-owned read slice that composes independent work-item and label capabilities. The RSC page reads through a server-only DAL, which authenticates the actor, injects capability ports, applies board policy, and returns serializable board DTOs.

tree.purpose: Valibot schemas for board filters, grouped results, visible label details, and stable failure types.
Board orchestration and policy: load work items and labels, hide archived items, group by status, attach visible labels, and discard inaccessible label associations.
Ports for reading work items and actor-visible labels; contains no persistence or framework imports.
Existing public work-item capability read contract.
Existing public label capability read contract that enforces actor visibility.
Work-item persistence adapter implementing the work-item read port.
Label persistence adapter implementing the label visibility/read port.
Server-only session/claims verification and actor context creation.
Structured logging and error reporting with request ID, actor scope, and failure category; excludes sensitive row data.
Server-only authenticated composition root; verifies auth, creates outbound adapters, invokes get-board, and maps failures to read-safe results.
Thin App Router RSC entrypoint; reads URL filters, calls the board DAL, and renders the board view or safe error state.
Pure/server-renderable board presentation using board DTOs; no persistence or capability imports.
User-safe unavailable/unauthorized rendering without exposing provider or authorization details.
Fake-port tests for board filtering, grouping, label attachment, inaccessible-label rejection, and dependency failures.
Auth boundary and safe failure/reporting tests.
Visibility enforcement, mapping, and persistence-error tests.
Board rendering tests for groups, labels, empty state, and safe error state.
Authenticated browser flow covering visible items, archived-item exclusion, label visibility, and unavailable reads.

flows: Board read: GET /board -> src/app/board/page.tsx -> src/dal/board/get-board-read.ts -> verify-request-actor.ts -> get-board.ts -> work-item reader and label reader -> Board DTO -> BoardView.tsx.

Work-item capability: get-board.ts -> work-item read port -> src/adapters/outbound/work-items/work-items-reader.ts -> work-item persistence. The board imports only the capability contract, never its persistence adapter directly.

Label capability: get-board.ts -> visible-label read port -> src/adapters/outbound/labels/labels-reader.ts -> label persistence, scoped to the actor. Returned labels are joined by ID; missing/inaccessible IDs are rejected from the board response.

Policy flow: fetch non-archived-capable work-item data, apply board-level archived filtering, group by status, collect referenced label IDs, fetch actor-visible label DTOs, attach only matching visible labels, and return stable grouped output.

decisions.choice: Board use case owns cross-capability policy.
decisions.rationale: Archived filtering, status grouping, label joining, and inaccessible-label handling are board concerns and must not couple work-items to labels.

decisions.choice: Board use case depends on local ports; DAL/inbound composition injects outbound implementations.
decisions.rationale: Use cases remain framework- and persistence-independent, while work-items and labels remain independently replaceable.

decisions.choice: Expose capability read contracts and a board DAL read entrypoint; expose no raw repositories or database rows.
decisions.rationale: The RSC needs a stable server-only read API, while capability ownership remains explicit.

decisions.choice: Re-check authentication in the board DAL and enforce label visibility in the label capability/read adapter.
decisions.rationale: Proxy protection is insufficient; every protected read must derive the actor server-side and fail closed.

decisions.choice: RSC-owned read through the server-only DAL; no TanStack Query.
decisions.rationale: The board is a read-heavy App Router page with no stated polling, realtime, or optimistic client lifecycle. Cache, if enabled, is owned by the DAL and scoped to actor/tenant and board inputs.

decisions.choice: Unauthorized reads return an authorization-safe result; capability or persistence failures return a generic unavailable state and emit structured telemetry.
decisions.rationale: Clients must not receive raw exceptions, provider details, or visibility information. Inaccessible label associations are omitted rather than leaked.

decisions.choice: Test board policy with fake ports, adapters against their lowest transport boundary, DAL auth/reporting separately, and the complete behavior with e2e.
decisions.rationale: Each test isolates the architectural boundary it protects.

risks: If labels are fetched with a service-role client, explicit actor/tenant predicates and database RLS must still prevent visibility escalation.
A cached board response must include actor/tenant scope and relevant filters in its cache key or tag; otherwise one actor’s visible labels could be exposed to another.
The board use case should define whether an invalid work-item status is rejected or placed in an explicit fallback group; this must be covered by its schema and tests.
Large boards may require bounded reads or pagination, but pagination policy should remain board-owned rather than leaking persistence details into the UI.
